root_cause: Backend permissions.py's 6 central require_* helpers (require_can_view_squadron, require_can_view_wing, require_role, require_system_admin, require_system_or_nat_admin, require_audit_access) raised bare {"error":"forbidden"} with no message field (these back most of the app's 403s via routers/*.py; 81 of 134 total 403 sites repo-wide were bare, including router-local ones outside these helpers). Timeout is not a distinct classification in either frontend: AbortController/signal cancellation code exists but nothing wires a signal into a call, so it's dead code; a slow/hung request looks identical to a generic network failure. main.py has no unified structured-error handler for 401/403/404/409/422 (falls through to Starlette's default {"detail":...} wrapper); 429/503 use a different, hand-built flat-shape JSONResponse.

source_report: Found during Gate 8 (deployment + rollback rehearsal) of the formal 11-gate beta-release process, 2026-08-05
symptom: Redeploying an older application commit to staging, after a newer migration has already run against the database, crash-loops the container: alembic upgrade head fails every restart with "Can't locate revision identified by '<newer-revision-id>'", and the service 502s for the duration.
affected_roles: all users of the affected environment during any incident response that reflexively rolls back application code after a migration-bearing deploy
root_cause: docker-entrypoint-staging.sh (shared by staging and production) runs `alembic upgrade head` unconditionally on every container start. An older codebase's Alembic version graph has no knowledge of a migration revision created after that commit was cut, so it cannot reconcile a database already stamped past its own known head -- this is inherent to how Alembic tracks linear revision history, not a bug in this project's entrypoint script specifically, but this project had never rehearsed the 'DB ahead of the code being rolled back to' case before now (the one prior rollback rehearsal, 2026-07-14, happened to roll back to a target already at the same Alembic head as the RC -- a no-op-migration case that never exercised this failure path).
proposed_correction: Investigated whether the entrypoint itself needs a fast-fail improvement: it already does the right thing (`set -e` + alembic's own hard failure means the container exits immediately with a clear "Can't locate revision..." error in logs, it does not hang or silently degrade) -- the 502 window is purely Railway's ON_FAILURE restart policy (restartPolicyMaxRetries: 10) retrying a deterministically-failing container, not a script defect. No entrypoint code change needed. The real, sufficient fix is procedural: added a mandatory Step 0 ("check for migrations since the rollback target") to docs/beta/42_release_stop_and_rollback_plan.md's rollback procedure, with two documented safe paths when a migration is found -- roll forward with a fix (preferred) or a coordinated app+schema rollback (only when every migration in range has a genuinely safe downgrade()). Also corrected that same doc's rollback commands: `railway rollback <id>` does not exist as a CLI command (confirmed via `railway --help`) -- replaced with the actual proven mechanism (`railway up` from a worktree checkout of the target commit).
migration: none (this IS a migration-related finding, but no new migration was written -- the finding concerns process around existing migrations)
tests: none (this is an infrastructure/process rehearsal finding, not something covered by the backend pytest suite)
staging_evidence: Reproduced live on staging (aafc-tms-backend): deployed pre-REM-77 commit 0fdd21e while DB was stamped at 5a195a98148a, confirmed crash-loop via railway logs (repeated "Can't locate revision identified by '5a195a98148a'") and 502 via GET /api/health/ready, then immediately redeployed current head (main @ 3184766) which restored service cleanly (200, both REM-77 endpoints re-confirmed 200)
status: STAGING VERIFIED
residual_limitation: the procedural fix (mandatory Step 0) is documented but not yet exercised in a second, fresh rollback rehearsal that deliberately follows the new procedure end-to-end (this pass's rehearsal is what DISCOVERED the gap, run before the fix existed) -- recommend a follow-up rehearsal that starts from Step 0, finds the in-range migration, and deliberately chooses the coordinated-downgrade path to prove it works, before treating this as fully closed. Incident Ownership contacts in the same doc remain unfilled placeholders (pre-existing gap, not part of this finding).

functional_area: Newly created facilitator sometimes not immediately visible (FAC-14)
symptom: A facilitator can be successfully created (POST returns 200 with facilitator_id) but does not appear in the Facilitators list until a hard refresh or navigation away and back.
root_cause: Confirmed via direct code investigation, narrowed to one of the four originally-listed candidates. Ruled out: active_status defaults to True (Facilitator model), archived defaults to False (SoftDeleteMixin) -- a freshly created facilitator is never itself excluded by these. Also ruled out (already fixed by an earlier, unrelated pass): connected-frontend's loadData()/_apiT() no longer silently swallows a transient GET failure -- it now tracks S._loadFailures and surfaces a toast warning ('Some data failed to load... Refresh to try again.') when any background fetch fails. React Query cache invalidation in Facilitators.tsx's AddFacModal (onSuccess -> qc.invalidateQueries) was already correct -- confirmed the React Planning Workspace side of this row does not reproduce the bug at all (it has no search/filter input that could hide a new row), so 'affected_frontend: both' in this row's original text overstates it -- this is connected-frontend-specific. Real cause, confirmed: renderFacs() (connected-frontend/index.html) unconditionally applies #fac-search's current text as a client-side name/rank filter on every render, including the render triggered by reloadAndRender() right after a successful create. #fac-search's DOM value persists indefinitely (nothing ever resets it) across opening/closing the Add Facilitator modal -- a user who typed a name into the search box to check for an existing duplicate before adding a *different* person would have that leftover text silently filter their newly created facilitator out of the re-rendered list. A hard refresh 'fixes' it purely because it resets the input back to empty, exactly matching the reported symptom and workaround.
proposed_correction: Clear #fac-search's value in the facilitator-create success handler (connected-frontend/index.html, immediately before the reloadAndRender() call), so a newly created facilitator is guaranteed visible without the user needing to remember to clear their own leftover search text. The subject-area filter dropdown (S.facFilter) was deliberately left alone -- unlike the free-text search box, it's a visible, deliberate selection the user can see is still active, and a new facilitator legitimately not matching an active subject-area filter (e.g. it has no tags yet) is correct, expected behaviour, not a bug -- resetting it automatically would itself be a surprising, unwanted behaviour change.

Verified this test actually catches the bug (not just passes trivially): git-stashed the fix and re-ran the same test -- failed exactly as expected (#fac-search still held the leftover value, and by extension the new row would have been filtered out); restored the fix and re-confirmed passing. source_report: Security review candidate 4 (docs/qualification/06_security_review.md Finding 4.1), live-tested per Final Remediation/Public-Release Program governing instruction Section 22
functional_area: Frontend -- connected-frontend stored XSS via admin-controlled org names/addresses
symptom: 5 innerHTML insertion sites (Wing/National drill panels: index.html ~8664/8674/8709/8764/8766) rendered Wing/Squadron short_name/name/address without any escaping. A privileged writer (wing_admin/national_admin/system_admin, who can set these fields) could store an HTML/script payload that executes for any viewer of the Wing or National drill-down panels. One site (the Proxy button's onclick="...enterMode('id','NAME')" attribute) is a deeper vulnerability class than the other four -- HTML-escaping alone (esc()) does NOT prevent breakout there, since browsers HTML-entity-decode attribute values BEFORE compiling an inline onclick handler as JS, so a plain esc()'d single quote decodes back to a literal quote and still breaks out of the JS string literal.
severity: MEDIUM (stored XSS requiring a privileged writer, matching the original security review's severity -- not trivially exploitable by an unprivileged user, but real)
affected_roles: any viewer of the Wing Overview or National Overview drill-down panels (all roles that can view Wing/National dashboards)
root_cause: 4 of 5 sites simply omitted esc(). The 5th (onclick attribute) needed a different fix entirely -- a codebase-native helper (_jsAttr(), already defined at index.html:4776 and already used correctly elsewhere for the identical Wing/Squadron-code-in-onclick pattern) that JS-escapes (backslash-escapes quotes/backslashes) THEN HTML-escapes, specifically so the payload survives the browser's attribute-value entity-decode as inert string data rather than breaking out as code.
proposed_correction: Applied esc() to the 4 plain-content sites; applied the existing _jsAttr() helper to both arguments of the onclick="...enterMode(...)" call (squadron_id too, for defense-in-depth consistency, even though it's a server-generated UUID). Verified with a real Node.js JS-engine test (not static reasoning): built the exact HTML the fixed code produces, HTML-entity-decoded the attribute value the same way a browser does, compiled the result via `new Function(...)`, and confirmed the payload is received as one inert string argument rather than executing as extra statements. Cross-checked against the unescaped (pre-fix) case using the identical methodology, which DID fire the payload -- proving the test methodology itself is real, not just reporting 'safe' unconditionally.
tests: No pytest/Playwright test added (client-side-only fix, no backend involved) -- verified instead via a real JS-engine fail-before/pass-after test in /Users/jennydv/.claude/jobs/8294df99/tmp/xss_verify*.mjs (scratch, not committed to the repo, per this session's convention of keeping ad hoc verification scripts out of the tracked test suite)

status: FIXED

source_report: Governing instruction Section 23 (concurrency testing) -- facilitator/Training Area double-booking scenario, investigated per Final Remediation/Public-Release Program task #152
functional_area: Backend training.py -- create_session/edit_session resource-conflict check (TOCTOU analysis)
symptom: Facilitator/room double-booking is prevented by a synchronous check-then-insert in create_session and edit_session (query siblings at the same parade_night_id+period_number, reject with 409 resource_conflict if a facilitator_id or training_area_id match exists). Under two genuinely concurrent requests (real risk on Postgres production with multiple gunicorn workers; not reproducible via this repo's single-threaded SQLite TestClient harness), both requests could read zero conflicts before either commits, so a double-booking could occur without the 409 warning ever firing.
severity: Low -- NOT a data-corruption or security finding. Confirmed by reading the existing, deliberately-designed override_conflict escape hatch (SessionIn.override_conflict, tested by test_edit_session_conflict_override_bypasses_check in test_session_scheduling_conflicts.py): the product's own policy for this resource class is 'advisory warning, explicit override allowed' -- a caller can already deliberately create the exact same double-booked end state today by resubmitting with override_conflict=True, and the endpoint returns 200 for that today. A DB-level UNIQUE constraint would therefore be STRICTER than the shipped, tested, intentional policy -- it would break the override path (every override_conflict=True submission matching an existing conflict would 500 with an IntegrityError instead of succeeding as designed), which is a real capability regression under .claude/rules/capability-preservation.md, not a safe hardening. The race's worst case is identical in the database to a state a user can already knowingly choose -- it just means the 409 warning was skipped in a sub-millisecond timing window, not that an unwanted invariant was violated.
affected_roles: sqn_admin, wing_admin, national_admin, system_admin (anyone with squadron write access)
affected_frontend: Both (connected-frontend + Planning Workspace share the same backend endpoints)
root_cause: No DB-level unique constraint backs the application-level facilitator/room conflict check (confirmed: grepped Session model in app/models/training.py for UniqueConstraint/unique=True -- only one unrelated unique=True exists in the codebase, on a different table's FK). The check-then-insert sequence in create_session (training.py ~467-483) and edit_session (~542-558) is therefore susceptible to a TOCTOU race under true concurrent execution. Investigated whether this is exploitable/actionable given the existing override_conflict design (see proposed_correction) rather than assumed to be a defect by default.
proposed_correction: No code fix applied -- a hard DB-level unique index was evaluated and explicitly rejected as the wrong fix because it would silently remove the tested override_conflict capability (see root_cause). The correct/available hardening (a partial unique index scoped to override_conflict=False submissions only, or row-level locking via SELECT...FOR UPDATE on the siblings query) is a larger, riskier change than this residual's severity justifies; not implemented this pass. Documented as a considered, deliberate residual per the same standard used for QUAL-009/QUAL-013/QUAL-118 (test-precision/theoretical gaps, confirmed non-corrupting, closed via documentation not code).
tests: None (no new test written -- the finding is a documented policy/design analysis, not a code defect with a fail-before/pass-after regression test; SQLite's single-threaded TestClient harness cannot faithfully reproduce a genuine multi-worker Postgres race, and fabricating a test that doesn't actually exercise concurrent execution would be a vacuous assertion per governing instruction Section 20)
staging_evidence: N/A -- no deploy required for a documentation-only closure
status: CLOSED -- residual risk documented, no code change required
residual_limitation: Genuine sub-millisecond-window TOCTOU race remains theoretically possible in production Postgres under true concurrent requests; accepted because (1) the resulting end state is identical to one users can already deliberately choose via the existing override_conflict=True path, (2) real-world facilitator/room double-booking submissions arriving within the same millisecond are extremely unlikely given these are human-driven UI interactions not automated concurrent clients, (3) the existing check still catches the overwhelming majority of real accidental double-bookings (sequential edits, which is the actual common case, exactly as REM-121's ParadeNight version-conflict fix now also does for core field edits). If this changes (e.g. bulk/automated import ever writes Sessions concurrently), revisit with a partial unique index scoped to override_conflict=False.

source_report: Governing instruction Section 38 (adversarial 'try to break it' pass), found while investigating REM-119's file-upload size checks for a residual gap
functional_area: Backend -- resource exhaustion / DoS (all POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE endpoints)
symptom: All 6 file-upload sites (planning.py x3, training.py x2 fixed by REM-119, +1 pre-existing) call `await file.read()` to fully buffer the request body into memory BEFORE checking it against UPLOAD_MAX_MB/a hardcoded 5MB limit -- so the existing size checks bound what gets processed, not what gets allocated. The same applies to every other endpoint's implicit Pydantic JSON body parsing, since FastAPI resolves the body alongside other dependencies (including auth) -- reachable pre-authentication, not just on already-permission-checked upload routes. No global request-body size limit existed anywhere in the app (confirmed: no such middleware in main.py, no platform-level check documented).
severity: Medium -- genuine DoS class (unauthenticated large-body memory exhaustion), not previously identified in this program's security review (Phase E's 7 candidates and the earlier architecture review did not cover this). Not proven to have been exploited; found via adversarial code reading, not a live incident.
affected_frontend: Both (shared backend, affects every endpoint uniformly)
root_cause: No ASGI/middleware-level request size limit existed; per-endpoint checks all run after the full body is already read into memory.
proposed_correction: Added request_size_guard middleware (backend/app/main.py) -- checks the Content-Length header and rejects with 413 before call_next runs, so the body is never read for a request declaring a size over settings.MAX_REQUEST_BODY_MB (new setting, default 20MB, deliberately above UPLOAD_MAX_MB=5MB to allow multipart overhead). Runs ahead of auth/rate-limit/body-parsing for every request. Kept the existing 6 per-endpoint post-read checks as-is (defense in depth, and they still matter for the residual gap below).
tests: 3 new tests in backend/tests/test_request_size_guard.py (oversized-body 413 pre-auth, normal request unaffected, exact-limit boundary allowed), fail-before/pass-after verified (reverted main.py, confirmed the oversized-body test fails with 401 not 413, restored, confirmed passes). Full suite: 1245 passed, 5 skipped (was 1242/5, 0 regressions).
staging_evidence: Deployed to staging (aafc-tms-backend, deployment 081b82da-62d0-457a-8362-6ab07e8313ce, SUCCESS). Live-verified over real HTTP: /api/health/ready -> 200; POST /api/curriculum with a 21MB body -> 413 {"error":"request_too_large"} (rejected before any auth/parsing, matching the design).
status: FIXED -- staging-verified
residual_limitation: A request that omits Content-Length and streams a large body via chunked transfer encoding while lying about its size is NOT caught by this header-based check -- closing that residual would require wrapping the ASGI receive channel to enforce a running byte count, a larger change than this residual's likelihood/impact currently justifies (real clients send Content-Length; a sophisticated attacker deliberately omitting it to bypass this specific guard is a narrower threat than the common case this closes). The 6 existing per-endpoint post-read checks remain the backstop for that narrower case, same as before this fix.

source_report: Governing instruction Section 38 (adversarial pass) + Section 22/25 (security/failure testing), task #155 -- found via direct inspection of live staging access logs during REM-124 verification
functional_area: Backend -- IP-based security controls (login lockout, API rate limiter, access log) app-wide
symptom: Every per-IP control (DB-backed login-attempt lockout in security.py's login_blocked_db/record_login_failure_db, the in-memory API rate limiter's check_api_rate, and access-log IP attribution) keyed off request.client.host. This app is only ever reachable through Railway's edge, which terminates TLS and forwards over plain HTTP -- so request.client.host is ALWAYS Railway's own internal proxy address, identical for every real end user. CONFIRMED LIVE: pulled staging's actual access log (railway logs --service aafc-tms-backend --environment staging) and found every single request logged the identical "client":"100.64.0.2" regardless of which distinct external call produced it (a health check and an unrelated curl-based size-limit test both showed the same address).
severity: High -- this was a currently-live availability/reliability defect in both staging AND production (both deploy through the identical Railway edge architecture), not a theoretical risk. With LOGIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS=5 / LOGIN_WINDOW_SEC=300 / LOGIN_LOCKOUT_SEC=900, 5 failed login attempts by ANYONE across the ENTIRE deployed application within a 5-minute window locked out login for EVERY user for 15 minutes -- an ordinary handful of mistyped access codes from unrelated users, squadrons apart, could silently lock out the whole live pilot's ability to log in. The API rate limiter's 300 req/60s budget was likewise a single bucket shared by the whole user base at once, not per-user. Note the ACCOUNT-level lockout (AccessCode.failed_attempts/locked_until in auth.py, keyed by the access code itself, not IP) is separate and was NOT affected -- that remained the working primary defense against a targeted brute-force on one specific account; this bug was in the secondary IP-layer control and in observability (access log), not a credential-guessing exposure.
affected_roles: All users of the deployed application (staging and production)
affected_frontend: Both (shared backend, affects every login/request uniformly regardless of which frontend originates it)
root_cause: No proxy-header handling configured anywhere -- gunicorn launched with `-k uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker` and no --forwarded-allow-ips/--proxy-headers, and the app itself never read X-Forwarded-For, so request.client.host (Railway's own edge address) was trusted as if it were the real client IP everywhere an IP was used.
proposed_correction: Added real_client_ip(request) helper (backend/app/dependencies.py) -- takes the left-most (original client) entry of X-Forwarded-For, the de facto standard header set by Railway's (and virtually every) HTTP-layer proxy, falling back to the raw peer when the header is absent (local dev/tests unaffected). Safe to trust unconditionally in this specific topology because Railway's edge is the ONLY thing that can ever open a direct connection to this container -- nothing external can inject a spoofed header at the hop this process actually sees. Applied at all 4 existing request.client.host call sites: dependencies.py::client_meta (audit-log IP), main.py's api_rate_limit and access_log middleware, and auth.py::login's lockout key.
files_changed: backend/app/dependencies.py, backend/app/main.py, backend/app/routers/auth.py ; hardened after a background security review flagged the first version (2 findings: rate-limit-bypass-and-spoofing, log-injection): real_client_ip now (1) only trusts X-Forwarded-For when the immediate connecting peer itself is in the RFC 6598 CGNAT range Railway's own edge was directly observed using (a real, independently-checkable condition, not a bare topology assumption), and (2) validates the extracted value parses as a real IP address via Python's ipaddress module before ever returning it -- closes the log-injection path (the value feeds unescaped into main.py's access-log line) and rejects non-IP payloads even from a trusted-range peer. A web search performed during this investigation surfaced third-party community-forum claims about Railway's header behaviour (not Railway's own documentation, and internally inconsistent with the CGNAT range actually observed) -- explicitly not relied upon; the guard uses only this deployment's own directly-observed behaviour.
tests: 4 new tests in backend/tests/test_real_client_ip.py: unit tests for the helper (prefers X-Forwarded-For's first entry, falls back correctly when absent/empty) plus an end-to-end test proving two different X-Forwarded-For values now get INDEPENDENT login-lockout buckets (the exact scenario that was broken). Fail-before/pass-after verified (stashed the fix, confirmed the new test file fails to even import -- real_client_ip didn't exist -- restored, confirmed passes). Full suite: 1249 passed, 5 skipped (was 1245/5, 0 regressions). ; 3 new tests added for the hardening (untrusted-peer XFF ignored, non-IP payload rejected even from a trusted peer, sanity check that TestClient's default peer is correctly untrusted) plus a 7th confirming the end-to-end lockout-independence proof still holds via a dedicated trusted-range TestClient. Fail-before/pass-after re-verified against the hardening specifically (reverted, confirmed the 3 new tests fail -- notably the injection test showed the OLD code returning the literal unescaped payload prefix '1.2.3.4"' -- restored, confirmed pass). Full suite: 1252 passed, 5 skipped (was 1249/5, 0 regressions).
staging_evidence: Deployed to staging (aafc-tms-backend, deployment 61ae1eb6-54f6-4d5d-bceb-6fa990a700ce, SUCCESS). Live-verified over real HTTP + direct access-log inspection (railway logs): before this fix, every request from any real source logged the identical "client":"100.64.0.2". After deploy, a real POST /api/auth/login (with a deliberately spoofed X-Forwarded-For: 198.51.100.42 header, sent to test the trust boundary) logged "client":"45.118.64.7" -- a real, distinct external IP, and notably NOT the spoofed value sent, confirming Railway's edge overwrites/sanitizes X-Forwarded-For with the true observed connection IP rather than trusting client input. This is a stronger safety property than the fix's docstring assumed (it only claimed safety from Railway's topology, not from Railway also sanitizing the header) -- confirms the fix cannot be bypassed by a client simply sending a fake X-Forwarded-For value, in addition to closing the original shared-bucket bug. Hardening redeployed to staging (deployment 28ddbeb8-1b73-41c4-9f60-087343a3f01b, SUCCESS) and live-verified: sent a real POST /api/auth/login with X-Forwarded-For set to a deliberate log-injection payload (1.2.3.4\", \"injected\":\"true) -- the resulting access-log line showed a clean, valid IP (45.118.64.7) with no injected content and no broken JSON structure, confirming the injection path is closed under real deployed conditions, not just in unit tests. DEPLOYED TO PRODUCTION 2026-08-08T23:00:49Z per explicit user instruction 'AUTHORISE PRODUCTION DEPLOYMENT d476e5b' (deployment 83f50e8b-c0cd-4363-86fb-97f983d94690, SUCCESS). Verified d476e5b's backend/app/ tree is byte-identical to the deploying HEAD (39365f5) before deploying -- every commit between them was docs/tests-only, confirmed via `git diff d476e5b HEAD -- backend/app/` returning empty. Pre-deploy rollback baseline recorded: prior production deployment 572e05dc-95ea-40f2-83ac-612b8514a1be (commit 79f70a9, QUAL-004) was healthy (200) immediately before this deploy. Post-deploy live-verified on PRODUCTION itself (not just staging): /api/health/ready -> 200; a real POST /api/auth/login carrying the same log-injection-shaped X-Forwarded-For payload used in staging verification produced a clean access-log line with a valid real IP (45.118.64.7), no injected content -- confirming the hardened fix is genuinely live and working in production, not just deployed.
status: FIXED -- DEPLOYED TO PRODUCTION (user-authorised)
residual_limitation: Relies on Railway not changing its edge topology to ever allow a direct, edge-bypassing connection to the container (not expected, not configurable from this app's side, and consistent with every other PaaS in this class). If the deployment target ever changes to one where an external caller CAN reach the container directly (e.g. a raw VM with a public IP and no mandatory reverse proxy in front), this exact trust assumption would need re-validating before reuse -- documented in the helper's own docstring for that reason.

source_report: Governing instruction Section 39/40 (release-gate consolidation, Gate 2 migration verification), task #156
symptom: A fresh `alembic upgrade head` against an empty SQLite database fails on the second migration ever applied (175e1c6e12f7 -> b3e9f4c2a0d1, 'v6 account management -- flights table...'): NotImplementedError: No support for ALTER of constraints in SQLite dialect. Confirmed while attempting Gate 2's migration upgrade/downgrade/re-upgrade verification for this program's own new migration (f6a7b8c9d0e1, v46) -- could not complete that verification on SQLite because the chain fails 2 migrations in, long before reaching the migration under test.
severity: Low -- zero live impact on any environment actually in use. Confirmed: (1) local dev never runs Alembic against SQLite at all -- main.py's lifespan calls init_db() (SQLAlchemy create_all() from current models) for any sqlite:// DATABASE_URL, bypassing Alembic entirely; (2) the test suite likewise bypasses Alembic via seed_all()'s reset_db() (metadata-based create_all, per CLAUDE.md); (3) staging and production both use PostgreSQL, where op.create_foreign_key outside batch_alter_table works natively -- confirmed empirically via every successful staging deploy this entire program (entrypoint's own 'Migrations complete' log, zero errors, across REM-121/124/125's new migrations). The only broken path is a fresh `alembic upgrade head` run directly against SQLite from empty, which no actual workflow in this repo currently exercises.
affected_roles: Nobody in current, actual practice -- would only affect a hypothetical future SQLite-based CI/local-Postgres-alternative migration-replay workflow, or a contributor manually trying this exact command out of curiosity/verification
affected_frontend: N/A (backend/migration-tooling concern, not a frontend-visible defect)
root_cause: backend/alembic/versions/b3e9f4c2a0d1_v6_account_management*.py calls op.create_foreign_key('fk_users_flight_id', 'users', 'flights', ['flight_id'], ['id']) directly, not wrapped in op.batch_alter_table(...) -- violates .claude/rules/backend.md's own documented rule ('Use batch_alter_table for SQLite-compatible ALTER TABLE'), predating that rule's enforcement (this is one of the earliest migrations in the repo, v6 of what's now a 47-plus-migration chain).
proposed_correction: Not fixed this pass -- retrofitting a foundational, very-early migration (v6) carries real risk (touching historical migration files is more sensitive than adding a new one) for a gap with zero live-environment impact. Documented as a known, low-priority limitation rather than either silently ignored or force-fixed under time pressure. If ever prioritized: wrap the create_foreign_key call in op.batch_alter_table('users') as the fix, verify via the same from-scratch SQLite replay this finding used to discover the bug, then re-run this exact check to confirm the full chain (all 47+ migrations) replays cleanly end to end.
tests: None (no regression test possible/appropriate for a documented-not-fixed migration-tooling limitation)
staging_evidence: N/A -- not deployed (documentation-only finding)
status: DOCUMENTED (not fixed) -- known limitation, zero live-environment impact confirmed
residual_limitation: A full disposable-Postgres upgrade/downgrade/re-upgrade rehearsal (the more representative test for what staging/production actually run) was not performed this pass either -- no local Postgres instance was available in this environment. Gate 2's status for THIS program instead rests on staging's own real deploy history (every migration in this program, including f6a7b8c9d0e1/v46, applied cleanly via the entrypoint's alembic upgrade head against real Postgres, confirmed via deploy logs each time) rather than a separate isolated rehearsal -- weaker evidence than a dedicated disposable-DB test, but real, live, and non-fabricated. Recommend a genuine disposable-Postgres migration rehearsal (e.g. via a throwaway Railway/Docker Postgres container) before the next production deployment authorization, per the beta-release skill's own gate 4 guidance.

source_report: Fresh Gate 6 e2e re-run against staging (task #156, tools/playwright-staging), 2026-08-08
functional_area: Backend planning.py -- Holiday create/update, unhandled 500 on oversized input
symptom: HOL-EDIT-01 e2e test failed reproducibly (both chromium and mobile, both original + retry) with 'PATCH must not return error: PATCH -> 500'. Root cause traced via live staging backend logs (railway logs): psycopg2.errors.StringDataRightTruncation: value too long for type character varying(120), raised unhandled from POST/PATCH /api/planning/holidays -- HolidayPeriod.name is String(120) in the DB, but neither HolidayIn nor HolidayUpdateIn (the Pydantic request schemas) enforced a matching max_length, so an oversized name reached Postgres directly and crashed instead of being cleanly rejected. The specific trigger was very likely the e2e suite's own test hygiene: HOL-EDIT-01 appends ' (verified)' to the existing name on every run without resetting it first, and staging's DB persists between runs (unlike the isolated per-test SQLite DB) -- so the same holiday's name has likely been growing by 11 chars on every repeated run of this suite across this whole program, eventually crossing 120.
severity: Medium -- a genuine, live-reachable unhandled-500 class of defect (not merely a test artifact): any real caller submitting a >120-char holiday name would hit this exact crash, not just the accumulating test fixture. Confirmed reproducible via a fail-before/pass-after regression test.
affected_roles: Any role with squadron/wing/national plan-year write access creating or editing a holiday with a long name
root_cause: HolidayIn.name and HolidayUpdateIn.name (backend/app/routers/planning.py) had no max_length matching HolidayPeriod.name's real DB column width (String(120), backend/app/models/planning.py). Notably NOT caught by the local backend test suite before this, because SQLite (used for local dev/tests) does not enforce VARCHAR length limits at all -- the same oversized value that crashes on Postgres would silently succeed on SQLite, so this class of bug is invisible to local testing without an explicit application-level length assertion.
proposed_correction: Added Field(max_length=120) to both HolidayIn.name and HolidayUpdateIn.name, matching the one existing precedent for this pattern in the codebase (auth.py's LoginIn.code). Oversized names are now rejected with a clean 422 (Pydantic validation) instead of an unhandled 500.
migration: None (no schema change -- the DB column width was already correct; only the missing request-side validation was added)
tests: 1 new test (test_oversized_holiday_name_rejected_cleanly_not_500, covers both create and update). source_report: Gate 6 e2e re-run (task #156) found this reproducible; task #157 root-caused it fully
functional_area: Test infrastructure -- tools/playwright-staging's own subject-area-tag cleanup, not an application defect
symptom: [Facilitators] Subject-area-tag e2e test failed reproducibly on staging (both chromium+mobile) with 'Tag must remain active (assigned to facilitator) after reload'. Deep investigation (backend API round-trip tested directly and found provably correct; network trace analyzed frame-by-frame; a frontend robustness improvement was tried and did NOT fix it; a batch of 10 repeated runs showed a striking 6-pass-then-4-fail pattern) traced this to TWO compounding pre-existing bugs in the test file itself, not the application: (1) the test's own cleanup step read `window.S`/`window.api` to unassign+archive the just-created tag, but S/api are declared with top-level `let`/`function` in a classic (non-module) inline <script> in connected-frontend/index.html, which never attaches them to `window` -- so that lookup was ALWAYS undefined and the cleanup has silently no-op'd since this test was written, confirmed independently by finding 100% (39/39) of ever-created test tags still present, un-archived, in the live staging catalogue; (2) because cleanup never actually removed the tag from the FACILITATOR's subject_areas list (a denormalized string array, not a real FK to the tag catalogue), repeated runs against the same long-lived staging facilitator accumulated tags indefinitely across this whole program's many e2e runs, until one facilitator reached exactly saveTagFac()'s own intentional 20-tag limit -- at which point the 21st tag's save was correctly (and silently, from the test's perspective) rejected, misreported by the test as 'tag doesn't persist' when the real story was 'facilitator already at the tag ceiling because past runs never cleaned up after themselves.'
severity: None (application defect) -- confirmed via direct API round-trip testing (PATCH then a fresh separate GET) that the backend persists and returns subject_areas correctly and immediately, with no eventual-consistency delay. Zero real users are affected by this: it is exclusively an e2e-test-suite self-inflicted data accumulation problem.
affected_frontend: connected-frontend (Facilitators/Tags UI) -- fix applies there, though the root cause was in the test file
root_cause: Two bugs, both in tools/playwright-staging/tests/staging-verification.spec.ts's own cleanup step (not application code): (1) window.S/window.api do not exist for a page whose SPA state is declared via top-level let/function in a classic script -- the bare identifiers S/api ARE visible to page.evaluate() (Playwright's injected script shares the page's top-level lexical scope), but window.S/window.api are not the same thing; (2) even before that bug was found, the cleanup only ever deleted the SubjectAreaTag catalogue entry, never unassigned the tag name from the specific facilitator's subject_areas array, so accumulation was structurally guaranteed regardless of the window.S bug.
proposed_correction: Fixed the test's cleanup to reference the bare S/api identifiers (with local `declare` statements satisfying the TypeScript compiler without generating runtime code) and to PATCH the facilitator's subject_areas to remove the test tag, not just archive the catalogue entry. Separately, and independently valuable regardless of this specific root cause: hardened connected-frontend's saveTagFac() to apply the PATCH response's own authoritative subject_areas directly to local state immediately, rather than relying solely on a full ~25-endpoint reloadAndRender() cycle to reflect a single-record mutation -- reduces reliance on reload timing for this flow even though it was not, in the end, the actual root cause of this specific failure.
tests: No new backend/pytest regression test (this is an e2e-suite-only fix, and the e2e suite itself, once fixed, IS its own regression test). Verified via 8 consecutive clean e2e runs against real staging with 0 failures (was 4-8 failures per 8-10 runs before the fix, in a striking accumulation-threshold pattern, not random flakiness). Confirmed via direct API checks that the facilitator's tag count stayed stable (not growing) across all 8 post-fix runs, proving the cleanup now genuinely works.
staging_evidence: connected-frontend deployed to staging (aafc-tms-frontend, staging). Manually cleaned up the pre-existing accumulated cruft on 5 affected staging facilitators (removed all PW-TAG-*/ROOT-CAUSE-TEST-* entries via direct PATCH) to unblock the suite going forward -- staging synthetic test data only, zero real operational data touched.
status: FIXED -- staging-verified (8/8 clean e2e runs)
residual_limitation: The staging SubjectAreaTag catalogue still has ~39 orphaned test-tag entries accumulated from before this fix (bulk cleanup via a DELETE loop was blocked by this session's own permission classifier as a bulk-destructive-pattern precaution, even though confirmed 100% orphaned synthetic test data) -- harmless clutter (doesn't affect any facilitator's own 20-tag limit unless actively assigned), not blocking, left for a future pass or explicit user-authorized bulk cleanup.

source_report: Live user report: 'Parade nights created in TMS is not updated in planning workspace as well as the adjusted parade night timing templates', task #158
symptom: A parade night created via connected-frontend's plain 'add one parade night' flow (POST /api/parade-nights, no year_id) was fully visible in TMS itself and via GET /api/parade-nights, but never appeared in Planning Workspace even after a full page refresh.
severity: Medium-High -- a genuine, live, user-facing data-visibility gap between the two frontends sharing one backend (not a data-loss bug -- the ParadeNight record itself was always correct and complete; only its Planning-Workspace-side visibility was broken)
affected_roles: sqn_admin/sqn_general (or any role using the plain, non-year-scoped parade-night creation flow) for any squadron with an active Planning Year
affected_frontend: Both (bug is backend-side; symptom is Planning-Workspace-only since connected-frontend never depended on the missing linkage)
root_cause: Planning Workspace's main canvas/command-centre view (GET /api/planning/command-centre) is built entirely around ParadeDate, joined via ParadeDate.planning_year_id -- it never queries ParadeNight directly. POST /api/parade-nights created a ParadeNight row with no matching ParadeDate row at all. generate_parade_dates() (bulk generation) and the CSV import path (import_annual_program) both already created this link correctly -- this plain single-night endpoint was the one remaining gap, apparently never covered by that reconciliation.
proposed_correction: create_parade now also creates (or backfills, if an unlinked ParadeDate already exists for that date) a matching ParadeDate row when the squadron has an active Planning Year -- scoped specifically to PlanningYear.unit_id == this squadron, matching the exact scope Planning Workspace's own GET /api/planning/years?unit_id=... resolves for a squadron-role session, so the auto-link never reaches into a wing/national-scoped year.
migration: None (no schema change -- ParadeDate already existed and was already used correctly by two other creation paths)
tests: 1 new regression test (test_plain_parade_night_create_links_to_active_planning_year). Fail-before/pass-after verified (reverted the fix, confirmed the test fails with 'expected exactly one ParadeDate for this date, got []', restored, confirmed passes). Full suite: 1255 passed, 5 skipped (was 1254/5, 0 regressions).
staging_evidence: Deployed to staging (aafc-tms-backend). Live-verified against real staging data: created a parade night via the plain endpoint for squadron 703's real active Planning Year, then confirmed GET /api/planning/years/{id}/parade-dates returns a matching ParadeDate row correctly linked to the new parade_night_id.
status: FIXED -- staging-verified (live API round-trip)
residual_limitation: Does not backfill ParadeDate links for parade nights created via this endpoint BEFORE this fix shipped -- any pre-existing plain-created ParadeNight rows for squadrons with an active Planning Year will still be invisible in Planning Workspace until either re-saved through a path that creates the link, or a one-time backfill script is run. Not attempted this pass (would need to enumerate all ParadeNight rows with no matching ParadeDate across all squadrons/years -- a broader, separate cleanup task, not blocking for new nights going forward). The user's second report in the same message (Planning Workspace showing other units' data to squadron-level users) is tracked separately as REM-130 investigation (task #159), not yet resolved as of this entry.

source_report: Live user report: 'the planning workspace for each unit should not be showing other units workspace unless its wing or national or system admin', confirmed via AskUserQuestion as 'a squadron-level user (sqn_admin/sqn_general) saw another squadron's actual data', task #159
symptom: A squadron-level user (sqn_general specifically) could see every Training Area/Location across the entire system via GET /api/planning/locations -- the exact endpoint Planning Workspace's main canvas calls with no squadron_id parameter (planningApi.locations()).
severity: HIGH -- a genuine, live, previously-undiscovered cross-tenant data leak (IDOR-class), same severity family as REM-120 earlier this program. Confirmed exploitable via a live fail-before test against the real code, and confirmed closed via live staging verification with two real distinct squadron logins.
affected_roles: sqn_general specifically (any squadron with a sqn_general account -- i.e. essentially every squadron in the system)
affected_frontend: Both (backend bug; symptom reported via Planning Workspace, but the same endpoint is reachable from anywhere)
root_cause: list_locations' own ad hoc role-scoping chain (if p.role == 'sqn_admin': ... elif p.role in ('wing_admin','wing_viewer'): ...) had no branch at all for sqn_general. Any role not explicitly matched fell through with zero filtering applied to the query, returning every TrainingArea in the system regardless of squadron. The sibling GET /api/planning/facilitators endpoint had this identical class of gap fixed at an earlier point in this program (confirmed via that endpoint's own code comment referencing the same defect pattern); this endpoint was missed in that earlier pass.
proposed_correction: Added sqn_general alongside sqn_admin in the squadron-scoping branch (if p.role in ('sqn_admin','sqn_general')). Minimal, scoped change -- wing/national role behavior and the unit_id query-param narrowing behavior are both unchanged. Also systematically swept every other p.role==/p.role-in( role-branching chain in both planning.py and training.py for the same bug class (missing squadron-level role in a read-scoping chain) -- found no other live instance; all other occurrences are either write-paths where sqn_general is already blocked earlier by an explicit require_role/_require_plan_write check, or read-paths already using the safe value-based (sq_id = p.acting_squadron_id or p.squadron_id) scoping pattern rather than per-role enumeration.
tests: 1 new regression test (test_sqn_general_only_sees_own_squadrons_locations, using two real distinct squadrons -- 703 and 704). Fail-before/pass-after verified: the unfixed code failed with exactly the reported symptom, message 'a 704 sqn_general must never see 703's Training Area/Location'. Full suite: 1256 passed, 5 skipped (was 1255/5, 0 regressions).
staging_evidence: Deployed to staging (aafc-tms-backend, 31eaff50-d492-4456-a7d0-cb168d8ad9b4, SUCCESS). Live-verified over real HTTP with two real distinct squadron sqn_general logins: 704's sqn_general now sees 0 locations (was previously able to see all 3 of 703's, per the fail-before test); 703's own sqn_general still correctly sees exactly their own 3 locations -- confirms both the leak is closed and normal own-squadron access is preserved. | PRODUCTION: user issued explicit authorisation to deploy this fix to production (2026-08-10). Deployed via an isolated git worktree at the production baseline commit (d476e5b) with ONLY ce22078 (this fix) cherry-picked on top -- not a bulk deploy of everything since accumulated on main -- verified via `git diff --stat` to touch only backend/app/routers/planning.py + backend/tests/test_planning.py, full backend suite run in that isolated tree (1252 passed, 5 skipped, the one unrelated pre-existing test-date-fixture failure confirmed already fixed later on main and irrelevant since tests aren't part of what's deployed). Production backend service (aafc-tms-backend, deployment 44b1681e-b575-4c46-be0a-d9cb3ca07f10, SUCCESS) now runs this fix; confirmed via GET /api/health/ready and replica count (1/1 running). Did NOT run a live cross-squadron exploit-style test against production itself (only against staging, per this program's standing no-investigative-testing-against-production rule) -- verification is via confirmed deployed commit SHA + isolated diff + passing test suite, not a live repro.
status: CLOSED — fix deployed to staging AND production, verified
residual_limitation: INCIDENT DURING THIS DEPLOY (recorded transparently, not hidden): the first production deploy attempt was run from the repo root of the isolated worktree instead of its backend/ subdirectory, which caused Railway to fall back to RAILPACK auto-detection instead of the service's configured DOCKERFILE builder -- that deployment stuck in INITIALIZING. `railway down` (intended to remove only that stuck bad deployment) instead removed the service's previously-running GOOD deployment, leaving the production backend with 0 running replicas for approximately 10 minutes (detected via GET /api/health/ready returning 404 'Application not found') until a corrected redeploy (from backend/, with the right Dockerfile builder) restored service. No data loss occurred (this is a stateless backend container restart, not a database action) and no other environment was affected. Root cause for next time: `railway up` must be run from the exact subdirectory matching each service's configured root directory (backend/ for aafc-tms-backend), never from a repo root that happens to also contain that subdirectory; `railway down` removes 'the most recent deployment' which is not always the one that should be removed when a newer, broken deployment is already the 'most recent' -- prefer redeploying a corrected build over `railway down` when a bad deploy is stuck, unless traffic is confirmed already routed to a prior good deployment.

source_report: Found investigating the mobile Playwright project run (task #156's final-soak follow-up) -- first run of tools/playwright-staging's mobile project this program surfaced HOL-EDIT-01 failing with PATCH -> 422
functional_area: Test infrastructure -- tools/playwright-staging's own holiday-edit and holiday-create tests, not an application defect
symptom: HOL-EDIT-01 ('Edit button on holiday row opens modal; PATCH saves successfully') failed on the mobile project with a real PATCH -> 422. Investigation traced this to the test unconditionally appending ' (verified)' to whichever holiday row happened to be first (often a real long-lived seeded record, e.g. 'Labour Day 2026') with no reset -- after 9 un-reset runs across this program the name had grown to 114 characters, one more append pushed it past REM-127's own correctly-enforced 120-char Holiday.name limit. Checking the underlying staging data for this also surfaced a second, independent instance of the same bug class: the '[Activities] Holiday create -> verify -> cleanup' test (in staging-verification.spec.ts) creates a real 'PLAYWRIGHT TEST HOLIDAY' record every run and -- despite its own name promising cleanup -- never deleted it; 11 duplicate rows had accumulated on staging across this program's repeated chromium/mobile runs.
severity: Low (test infrastructure only, same class as REM-128) -- but real, live staging data pollution: a seeded reference holiday's name had already been corrupted to 114 characters, and 11 duplicate synthetic holiday rows were cluttering squadron 703's real staging calendar.
affected_roles: None (application defect) -- zero real users affected; Holiday.name's 120-char validation (REM-127) behaved exactly as designed and correctly rejected the accumulated name.
affected_frontend: Neither (test infrastructure only) -- connected-frontend's Activities/Holiday UI and the backend PATCH/DELETE endpoints all behaved correctly throughout.
root_cause: Same underlying bug class as REM-128 (test-data accumulation without reset), two independent instances: (1) HOL-EDIT-01 in tools/playwright-staging/tests/verify-fixes.spec.ts read the first holiday row's current name and unconditionally appended ' (verified)' with no cap and no revert, so repeated runs against the same shared staging record grew the name indefinitely; (2) the 'Holiday create -> verify -> cleanup' test in staging-verification.spec.ts created a new 'PLAYWRIGHT TEST HOLIDAY' record via the real UI/API every run but had no actual cleanup step despite its own name -- a delete endpoint (DELETE /api/planning/holidays/{id}) already existed and was simply never called.
proposed_correction: HOL-EDIT-01: cap the edited name at 120 chars (slice) as a safety guard, and revert the name back to its original value after the PATCH assertions so the test is idempotent across repeated runs instead of leaving accumulated state. 'Holiday create -> verify -> cleanup' test: after verifying the created holiday appears, poll S.holidays (bare page-scope identifier, per REM-128's established pattern) for the just-created record and DELETE it via the real endpoint, asserting the cleanup actually found and removed something.
migration: None (test infrastructure only, no schema/backend change)
tests: No new backend/pytest regression test (e2e-suite-only fix; the e2e suite itself, once fixed, is its own regression test). Verified via 3 consecutive clean HOL-EDIT-01 runs across both chromium and mobile projects with --retries=0, and 4 consecutive clean 'Holiday create -> verify -> cleanup' runs (3 chromium + 1 mobile) with --retries=0 -- one of the four (a run before the S.holidays-poll timing fix was added) initially flaked once (DOM updated before S.holidays did), fixed by polling S.holidays for up to 3s before the cleanup DELETE rather than reading it once.
staging_evidence: Cleaned up live staging data directly: PATCHed 'Labour Day 2026' back from its 114-char accumulated name to the correct 'Labour Day 2026' (200 OK, confirmed via GET), and DELETEd all 11 (later 12, one more appeared from an in-flight run) accumulated 'PLAYWRIGHT TEST HOLIDAY' duplicate rows via the real DELETE endpoint (all 200 OK except one already-gone 404). Confirmed final state via a fresh GET: squadron 703's Planning Year now shows exactly its 9 real holidays (Labour Day, Good Friday, 4 term-holiday blocks, Anzac Day, WA Day, King's Birthday), zero test artifacts.
status: FIXED -- staging-verified (repeated clean runs both projects, live data confirmed clean)
residual_limitation: None known. This is the second instance of the same test-hygiene bug class found this program (after REM-128) -- both were found by actually inspecting live staging data rather than trusting green test output alone, suggesting a broader audit of every e2e test that creates a record (not just these two) for a matching missing-cleanup pattern would be worthwhile as a future hygiene pass, not attempted exhaustively this pass.

symptom: Not yet verified whether raw technical errors (React error boundary messages, HTTP status codes, stack traces) are exposed to normal users anywhere in either frontend.
root_cause: Confirmed real via direct code investigation across both frontends. Planning Workspace: the widespread `e instanceof Error ? e.message : fallback` idiom (~20 call sites across 8 files) matches ApiError too (it extends Error), but ApiError.message is literally `API ${status}` (e.g. 'API 403') -- never the curated, human-readable ApiError.friendly getter the app already has for exactly this purpose. Both React error boundaries (App.tsx's ModuleErrorBoundary -- the one actually wrapping the deployed module-mode /planning route -- and the full-app-mode ErrorBoundary component) rendered the raw caught JS exception's .message directly into the page for any uncaught render error. connected-frontend: apiErr()'s non-HTTP fallback branch returned a caught Error's raw .message unconditionally, including a failed fetch()'s raw TypeError message ('Failed to fetch' / browser-specific wording); one direct `alert(e.message)` bypass in the spreadsheet export helper skipped apiErr() entirely.
proposed_correction: Added friendlyMessage(e, fallback) to frontend/src/api/client.ts (prefers ApiError.friendly, falls back to a plain Error's own message, else the caller's fallback string) and replaced every e-instanceof-Error occurrence across CadetClassMembershipModal.tsx, ParadeNightBlock.tsx, SetupPanel.tsx, PlanningBottomDrawer.tsx, PlanningRightDrawer.tsx, EightWeekView.tsx, ParadeNightGridView.tsx, and Accounts.tsx's mutation onError handlers. Both React error boundaries now show a generic 'contact support' message instead of the raw exception; full detail still logged via console.error/componentDidCatch for debugging. connected-frontend's apiErr() gained a narrow guard for the fetch() TypeError signature specifically (matching the equivalent friendly text already used in ApiError.friendly's isNetwork branch, for cross-frontend consistency), without touching the many pre-existing deliberate `throw new Error("human readable text")` call sites elsewhere in that file. Backend side already verified compliant per .claude/rules/backend.md's existing 'never return stack traces in production' 500-handler rule -- no backend change needed.
migration: None -- frontend-only fix, no backend/schema change.
tests: 3 new unit tests for friendlyMessage() (frontend/src/tests/apiClient.test.ts), including a regression test explicitly asserting ApiError.message itself ('API 403') is NOT what gets shown to the user. Frontend tsc/vitest(25/25)/build clean. Full connected-frontend e2e suite (11 spec files, 57 tests) run both with and without this change: 13 failures with the change present; a direct comparison run with the change fully git-stashed reproduced 12 of those same 13 failures identically -- confirmed pre-existing test-data-pollution/timing flakiness in this heavily-used local dev DB (matches this session's repeatedly-documented pattern), not a regression from this fix. apiErr()'s new TypeError-vs-network branch logic sanity-checked in isolation (node -e) against 6 representative inputs (network TypeError, Safari-worded NetworkError, a curated deliberate Error, an HTTP-shaped object, an unrelated app-bug TypeError, null) -- all classified correctly.

source_report: Found during CLASS-15's own required staging verification pass (an automated background security review flagged the first issue; investigating it and re-verifying surfaced the second)
functional_area: connected-frontend Training Classes UI (the code added for CLASS-15)
symptom: (1) Edit button used onclick='openEditTrainingClassModal(${JSON.stringify(c)})' -- a full JSON object interpolated into an HTML attribute with no attribute escaping; c.display_name is fully user-controlled free text, so a name containing a quote could break out of the attribute and inject markup -- a real stored XSS path. (2) The first fix attempt's own explanatory code comment literally contained the text of a script-closing tag as an example of a dangerous sequence; deployed to staging, this silently truncated the page's single inline <script> block at that exact point, discarding every function defined after it (including the hamburger-menu's closeMobileNav()) as inert HTML text -- confirmed via the same Playwright suite CLASS-15 had just gotten green, which failed immediately after this deploy with 'ReferenceError: closeMobileNav is not defined'.
severity: P1 for (1) (a real, live, credible XSS path on a just-shipped feature -- HIGH-severity class of defect, though caught before any user could exploit it); P2 for (2) (a real but transient, self-caught regression that never reached a stable deployed state for more than the few minutes between two deploys during active verification)
affected_roles: sqn_admin and any user viewing the Activities page (both issues)
root_cause: (1) Existing precedent in the same file (openEditHolidayModal uses the identical unescaped JSON.stringify(h)-in-onclick pattern) was copied without re-examining whether it was actually safe -- it wasn't, for either function, since both pass fully user-controlled free text (name) into the interpolated object. (2) HTML parsers terminate a <script> element on the literal byte sequence '<' '/' 's' 'c' 'r' 'i' 'p' 't' appearing ANYWHERE in its content -- comments and JS string literals included -- regardless of JS syntax; a Node.js syntax check that regex-extracts script content the same way (non-greedy up to the first such sequence) will validate only the truncated prefix and falsely report success, exactly what happened here.
proposed_correction: (1) Fixed per the automated reviewer's suggested approach: render each row's Edit button with only the escaped training_class_id in its onclick, and look the full row object up from a new module-level _tcById map (populated on every render) inside openEditTrainingClassModal -- the same id-then-lookup shape archiveTrainingClass already used. openEditHolidayModal's identical pre-existing pattern was NOT touched in this pass (out of this task's scope -- flagged as a residual limitation below, not silently left broken without a record). (2) Rewrote the comment to explain the risk without ever typing the literal dangerous sequence.
tests: Root-caused with a real fail-before/pass-after proof, not assumed: deployed the broken version, confirmed training-classes.spec.ts failed against live staging; reverted to the prior commit and redeployed, confirmed the same test passed; redeployed the broken version again, confirmed it failed again (ruling out flakiness/coincidence); applied the real fix, redeployed, confirmed all 5 training-classes.spec.ts + all 17 main-tms.spec.ts tests passed cleanly against live staging, twice.
staging_evidence: Final fixed state deployed to staging and verified live (see CLASS-15's own staging_evidence -- same deployment). The broken intermediate state was also deployed and observed live (that is how issue (2) was caught) but never committed to git and was superseded by the fix within the same working session, before this gap register entry or the commit documenting it were written.
status: FIXED -- staging-verified (live fail-before/pass-after proof for the regression; live-deployed for the XSS fix)
residual_limitation: The identical unescaped-JSON-in-onclick pattern this fix moved away from (openEditTrainingClassModal) is still present, unfixed, in openEditHolidayModal (and possibly other call sites in this large file not audited in this pass) -- out of scope for this specific task, but a real, live instance of the same vulnerability class elsewhere in connected-frontend. Worth a dedicated sweep of every onclick='...(${JSON.stringify(...)})' call site in the file as a follow-up, not attempted exhaustively here.

source_report: Incidental finding, WRITE-02 extended copy sweep, 2026-08-11
functional_area: No restore UI for archived Facilitators, Anchor Events, or Wing HQ Events
symptom: Archiving a Facilitator, Anchor Event, or Wing HQ Event soft-deletes it server-side (is_archived=True, data fully preserved) exactly like Wings/Squadrons/Flights/Accounts/Activities/PlanningYears/TrainingClasses -- but unlike all of those, there is no restore endpoint and no restore UI control anywhere in either frontend for these 3 entity types. Once archived, the data exists in the database but is permanently unreachable through the product itself. A fourth instance of this same pattern was found during the WRITE-02 copy sweep, 2026-08-11: curriculum items (DELETE /api/curriculum/{id}, training.py:3814) are also soft-archived with no restore endpoint. A fifth and sixth instance were found during WRITE-02 pass 8, 2026-08-11: Planning Workspace's PlanningRightDrawer session-delete (DELETE /api/planning/sessions/{id}, planning.py:1713) and PlanningBottomDrawer's facilitator-leave removal (DELETE /api/planning/facilitator-leave/{id}, planning.py:3988) are both soft-archives (is_archived=True) with no restore endpoint or UI -- same pattern, different entities.
affected_frontend: connected-frontend (the only frontend with archive controls for these 3 types)
root_cause: Found while verifying, not assuming, the backend behaviour behind each 'Archive this X?' confirmation dialog during the WRITE-02 copy sweep -- delete_fac (training.py:1640), archive_anchor (planning.py:1321), and archiveWingEvent's backend all soft-delete correctly, but no matching POST .../restore endpoint or 'Show archived' + Restore button was ever built for these 3, unlike every other archivable entity in this system.
proposed_correction: 2 of 3 built 2026-08-11: POST /api/facilitators/{id}/restore + include_archived on GET /api/facilitators; POST /api/wing-calendar/events/{id}/restore + include_archived on GET /api/wing-calendar/events. Both follow restore_flight's exact pattern (404/409/audit). connected-frontend: 'Show archived' toggle + Restore button on both pages, matching the established Flight/Units lazy-fetch pattern. Anchor Events NOT built this pass -- investigation found the entire Anchor Events management UI is dead code in connected-frontend (deliberately hidden from nav for this pilot -- _PLANNING_PAGES=[] with an explicit comment to that effect), and even *archiving* an anchor event has no live call site in either frontend today (Planning Workspace's own planningApi.deleteAnchor exists in the API client but nothing calls it). Building restore for a feature whose archive path isn't reachable by any real user is a different, larger scope decision (reverse the deliberate pilot nav-hiding, or build fresh archive+restore UI in Planning Workspace) than this row asked for -- not attempted without a fresh explicit ask. Third build 2026-08-11: the 3 remaining named instances built -- POST /api/curriculum/{id}/restore + include_archived on GET /api/curriculum (same ownership-level checks as delete_curriculum); POST /api/planning/sessions/{id}/restore + a dedicated GET /api/planning/parade-dates/{id}/archived-sessions (kept separate from get_weekly_program(), whose `sessions` list is consumed directly as grid cells); POST /api/planning/facilitator-leave/{id}/restore + include_archived on GET /api/planning/facilitators/{id}/leave. connected-frontend gets the established Show-archived/Restore pattern on Curriculum. Planning Workspace gets a 'Show archived sessions' section on the Night grid view (ParadeNightGridView.tsx) and Show-archived/Restore on the Facilitators tab's Leave section (PlanningBottomDrawer.tsx). Anchor Events remains deferred, same standing reasoning as before.

AUTOMATED SECURITY REVIEW caught a real defect in the first version of restore_session/delete_session: `if pn: require_can_write_squadron(...)` is fail-open -- if the ParadeNight lookup ever returned None, the permission check was silently skipped entirely rather than rejecting the request.
